AOSP GSI Insight can rebuild this APK so Android accepts it, and sign it with a key that stays on this device. The file you picked is not modified. Changes:
Raise the target SDK from %1$d to %2$d.
Install under a new package ID: %1$s
The file itself already meets this Android version\'s requirements. You can still install it next to the original:
Install next to the original (new package ID, separate data)
Without a new package ID the app would have to replace the installed original, which only works if both are signed with the same key. Otherwise uninstall the original first (its data is lost).
Raising the target SDK changes how Android treats the app (runtime permissions, background limits, storage access). Old apps may crash or lose features.

The signing key is created and kept on this device. If you uninstall AOSP GSI Insight or reset the device, apps patched with it can no longer be updated by new patched builds; they would have to be reinstalled.
The resource compiler (aapt2) is not part of this build, so fixing is unavailable.
Split bundles (.apks, .xapk, .apkm) cannot be fixed yet: all parts must be signed together.
Showing the fixed APK that AOSP GSI Insight just built and signed.
Open AOSP GSI Insight to install it.

This package is closed-source Google software (GApps). Google licenses it to device makers only, so this app does not provide, host or sell it. It only inspects and installs a file you obtained yourself; check that you are allowed to use it.

If installing fails with a permission or provider conflict, the system image probably already contains a stub (GApps, microG) that declares the same permissions. Remove or disable that package first; renaming the permissions would break the app.
Open alternatives: microG for Play Services, Aurora Store or F-Droid for apps, and the WebView that ships with AOSP.
AOSP GSI Insight is free for inspecting, checking, installing and fixing a single APK. Donations pay for the manager itself; they never unlock downloads of proprietary software.
No advertising SDK is declared in the manifest.
Detected from manifest components and meta-data only; the app code is not scanned, so this is a lower bound. A game engine alone does not prove that an app shows ads.

This package ID is in Google\'s namespace (com.google.android.*), but that does not prove the app comes from Google: third-party apps sometimes use it. Check the signing key in the Signatures card before trusting it.
A new APK will be built and signed with this device\'s key. The file you picked is not changed. Raising the target SDK can change how the app behaves.
The manifest says this APK was distributed through Google Play.
This file is one piece of an app delivered as splits (Google Play). On its own it may be incomplete or fail to start; install the whole bundle.
The other splits are marked as required.
This is only what the manifest claims. Anyone can write it, so it is not proof of origin; check the signing key in the Signatures card.
Inspects, checks and fixes APKs for AOSP GSI devices (Android 7–16).
What this app does not do

It does not host, bundle or sell proprietary Google software (Play Store, Play Services, WebView). It analyzes and installs files you supply, and signs fixed copies with a key that stays on your device. Check that you are allowed to use the files you open.
License texts and notices are in the project repository (third_party/).
Targets below API %1$d: this Android would refuse a new install of it.
Values of the manifest\'s application element as Android reads them; unset attributes show their default. usesCleartextTraffic is on by default for apps targeting API 27 or lower.
Security: the APK is analyzed locally. AOSP GSI Insight does not install, run or modify the selected file.
Found from manifest components, meta-data and permissions only. A match shows the SDK is declared, not that it is used; an SDK that declares nothing is missed.
no native code (runs on any ABI)

Use this when an archiver app or another tool saved the APK again and Android now says it is corrupt or cannot be parsed. The content is not changed: the archive is rebuilt in the layout Android requires and signed again with this device\'s key.

It does not raise the target SDK or rename the package (use Fix for that), and a truncated or unreadable file cannot be repaired. The new signature differs from the original, so an installed copy signed by someone else will not update.
Bundles (.apks, .xapk, .apkm) cannot be repaired as a whole. Extract the base APK and open that.
A new APK will be built and signed with this device\'s key. The file you picked is not changed.
Native libraries and resources that live in split APKs of this app are not read.
Tap an app to inspect it.
The stored key could not be read, so the device key is used instead. Create or import a key again.

Patched and repaired APKs are signed with this key. The device key stays inside the Keystore: it cannot be exported and is deleted with the app, after which apps you patched cannot be updated by new patched builds. An exportable key can be saved to a password-protected .p12 file and imported after a reinstall. Anyone who has the file and its password can sign apps as you, so keep it private. Importing reads PKCS #12 (.p12, .pfx) files.
A new key replaces the one in use. Apps already signed with the previous key cannot be updated by builds signed with the new one; they would have to be reinstalled.
Go back to the device key?
The stored key is removed from this app. Export it first if you still need it.
Choose a password for the file. You need it to import the key again.
Enter the password of the PKCS #12 file. The key replaces the one in use.
A new exportable key is now in use.
The key was saved. Keep the file and its password safe.
The key was imported and is now in use.
The device key is in use again.
The file is not a readable PKCS #12 key file. If it was made by a recent desktop keytool, export it again with legacy encryption (keytool -J-Dkeystore.pkcs12.legacy).
The file holds no private key with a certificate.
The certificate in the file does not belong to its private key.
Only an exportable key can be exported.
Tap an activity to open it. Long-press any row to copy its name. Without root, Android only opens activities the app exports; the rest are refused.

Dialer codes this app listens for, read from its manifest. Dial opens the system dialer with the code filled in; the dialer decides whether to run it, and some dialers ignore secret codes. Long-press a row to copy the code.
Filter by app, package or code

Dialer codes (*#*#code#*#*) that installed apps declare in their manifests. Dial opens the system dialer with the code filled in; the dialer decides whether to run it, and some dialers ignore secret codes. Long-press a code to copy it.
